specs.value: pH, high range pH, ammonia, nitrite, nitrate (no GH or KH)
7 test solutions, 4 test tubes with caps, holding tray, laminated color card, instructions

variants.name: API Freshwater Master Test Kit (combined kit)

specs.value: pH, high range pH, NH3/NH4, NO2, NO3; 800+ tests

variants.name: API single liquid kits sold separately in Vietnam

specs.value: Sold separately; not part of the Master kit

fits.fact: Designed for freshwater aquariums. Do not use it for saltwater tanks.
It does not measure hardness, so planted or shrimp tanks that need GH/KH readings require the separate API GH & KH kit.
In planted tanks dosed with KNO3 fertilizer, nitrate readings come out higher.
A Vietnamese retailer's guide calls it one of the most trusted kits for checking pH, ammonia, nitrite and nitrate.

usage.fact: Fill a tube with tank water, add the drops for one parameter, then compare the color with the card.
API recommends testing weekly, and also whenever fish look unwell.
Shake reagent bottles hard. Invert the capped tube gently for the stated time, holding the cap with a finger.
Rinse the tubes right after each test so they don't stain.
Shake nitrate bottle #2 thoroughly because its crystals settle. The mixed sample also needs about a minute of shaking.
Hold the bottle vertically and upside down when dropping. Fill the sample to the white line, measured at the bottom of the meniscus.
Tap water tested straight from the faucet can show a high pH from dissolved CO2. Letting it stand for 24 hours gives a more representative reading.

issues.fact: Nitrate is the most error-prone test. Results vary with shaking technique, and the 40 and 80 ppm colors look nearly the same.
A hobbyist found its nitrate readings much higher than test strips gave.
An expired nitrate kit read 0 every time, while two other brands showed nitrate present.
The reviewer says reagents older than about 3–4 years may give poor results, especially nitrate.
The ammonia test reads ammonia and ammonium together. Tap water containing ammonium can produce a small reading in a new tank.
There are only 4 tubes, and the instructions are long. Color-blind users may find the color matching hard.
Despite the handbook title, this kit does not test GH or KH. Those need the separate API GH & KH kit.

alternatives.model: Single test kits (pH, NO2, NO3, NH3/NH4, GH&KH)
alternatives.why: Sold separately at a Vietnamese shop, from 150,000 to 250,000 đ each. You can buy only the tests you need and add GH/KH.
Liquid kit that adds KH to pH, NO2, NO3 and NH4. Described as accurate and usable in freshwater or saltwater.
Faster and simpler strips that include GH, KH and chlorine, but less accurate than liquid kits.
